 Travel Information

Pakistani Nationals in Afghanistan Are Advised to Take into Consideration Following Do’s & Dont’s While Living in Afghanistan

Dos

  • Keeping in view the Security situation in Afghanistan Pakistani nationals are advised to minimize their visits and only undertake journey when unavoidable
  • Respect local customs, traditions and laws
  • Promote and project interests of the companies/organizations that you work for
  • Present and project a good national image of Pakistan by adhering to and reflecting our national values
  • Be sensitive to the experience that Afghans have endured due to protracted wars
  • Show respect and regard for current leadership
  • Strike a chord of brotherhood, common cultural, religious and historical heritage during interaction with the locals
  • The local dress code may be observed
  • Be cognizant of own visa validity/duration
  • While moving in Afghanistan, always register with, and report to, the Pakistani representation (Embassy or Consulate) and maintain close contact
  • In case of any emergency or accident, the focal person of Pakistan Mission may be contacted immediately

Donts

  • Avoid taking part in political activities
  • Avoid illegal stay without passport/valid visa
  • Avoid political and religious discussions
  • Avoid publicizing travel, including on social media
  • Avoid un-necessary social media discussion
  • Abstain from indulging in any political discussion or debate that might hurt the sentiments and feelings of the locals
  • Avoid mentioning topics of ethnic tension or warfare
  • Be aware that many individuals might have strong opinions about faith and any debate on the same can potentially lead to a heated argument or unpleasant situation
  • Follow the local laws, rules and regulations, and abstain from taking photographs of sensitive places and installations
  • Avoid photographs of local people without their consent
  • You are not allowed to use or bring in any banned/contraband items, drugs, alcohol or pork products through airports and other entry points
  • Visits to places of congregation may be avoided in the interest of Public safety
